Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

mixedsubjects 1.1.0

This release brings the package in line with the finite-sample theory in the Supplementary Information of the accompanying paper. Standard errors change for all four cross-fit estimators, and point estimates change slightly for three of them. Analyses run with 1.0.0 should be rerun.

Variance of the cross-fit estimators

  • New analytic variance for msd_ppi(), msd_dt(), msd_dip_pp() and msd_dt_dip(). The variance is now assembled fold by fold: each fold’s fixed-tuning variance is evaluated at the tuning used in that fold with that fold’s own moments, the shared-unlabeled covariance uses the realized fold tunings, and a new second-order cross-fold term accounts for the dependence between each fold’s tuning estimate and the labeled data it was estimated on. The cross-fold term is estimated in closed form from third central moments. Standard errors are slightly larger than in 1.0.0, most visibly with small labeled samples and skewed outcomes or predictions.
  • additional$variance_components reports the three pieces of the new variance (fold_variances, cross_unlabeled, cross_fold), which sum to the reported variance. additional$variance_fixed_lambda reports the 1.0.0 fixed-tuning plug-in for comparison.

Tuning from labeled data only (changes point estimates)

  • msd_dip_pp() and msd_dt_dip() now estimate their tuning parameters from labeled data only. In 1.0.0 the second moments of the predictions that enter the tuning rule with weight 1/m were estimated from the unlabeled pool, which made the tuning depend on data the estimator is evaluated on. They are now estimated from the labeled tuning folds (every labeled unit carries both predictions), so the tuning is independent of the unlabeled pool and of the fold it is applied to, as the unbiasedness results require. Point estimates and tuning parameters from these two functions change slightly.

Fold weights for D-T (changes point estimates when folds are unequal)

  • msd_dt() now combines the fold-specific arm means with weights equal to each fold’s share of the arm’s labeled units, instead of equal weights. The two coincide whenever each arm’s labeled sample size is divisible by n_folds; otherwise point estimates change slightly. The weights are returned in additional$fold_weights, and the reported lambda is the correspondingly weighted average of the fold tunings.

Unchanged

  • msd_dim(), msd_greg() and msd_dip() are unaffected. Point estimates from msd_ppi() are unchanged.

mixedsubjects 1.0.0

CRAN release: 2026-07-02

  • Initial release.
  • Seven estimators for the average treatment effect in mixed-subjects designs: Difference-in-Means, GREG, PPI++, Doubly-Tuned (D-T), Difference-in-Predictions (DiP), DiP++, and D-T DiP.
  • Variance estimation via delta-method or fold-respecting bootstrap.
  • Optimal design selection for allocating budget between human observations and LLM predictions.
